title.value: On the Spinor Genus and the Distinguishing Lattice Isomorphism Problem
On the Spinor Genus and the Distinguishing Lattice Isomorphism Problem

abstract.value: This paper addresses the spinor genus, a previously unrecognized classification of quadratic forms in the context of cryptography, related to the lattice isomorphism problem (LIP). The spinor genus lies between the genus and equivalence class, thus refining the concept of genus. We present algorithms to determine whether two quadratic forms belong to the same spinor genus. If they do not, it provides a negative answer to the distinguishing variant of LIP. However, these algorithms have very high complexity, and we show that the proportion of genera splitting into multiple spinor genera is vanishing (assuming rank n ≥ 3). For the special case of anisotropic integral binary forms (n = 2) over number fields with class number 1, we offer an efficient quantum algorithm to test if two forms lie in the same spinor genus. Our algorithm does not apply to the HAWK protocol, which uses integral binary Hermitian forms over number fields with class number greater than 1.
